content: The TAF12 protein, also known as Transcription Initiation Factor TFIID Subunit 12, is encoded by the TAF12 gene in humans. Function: The regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II involves the basal transcription machinery, which is a collection of proteins. These proteins, together with RNA polymerase II, assemble into complexes that are influenced by transactivator proteins. These transactivator proteins bind to cis-regulatory elements located near the transcription start site. Some modulatory proteins interact directly with the basal transcription complex, while others act as bridging proteins that connect transactivators to the basal transcription factors. Among the associated factors, some are weakly attached, whereas others are tightly associated with the TATA-binding protein (TBP) within the TFIID complex. The tightly associated factors include the TAF proteins. Different TAF proteins are thought to mediate the activity of specific transcriptional activators for various gene promoters and RNA polymerases. TAF12 directly interacts with TBP as well as with TAF2I. Interactions: TAF12 has been demonstrated to interact with TAF9 and the transcription initiation protein SPT3 homolog.
